chapter_theme: The subtle five-letter mantra: the letters stand for Siva, his Shakti or grace, the soul, concealment and impurity, and chanting சிவாய, with நம (taken as the bonds) dropped, or simply சிவசிவ, removes the bonds and karma, turns the body to gold, and ends birth in becoming Siva.
structure_note: Two verses on the letters as a body of grace (2709, 2710), three on the five letters as the categories and the dropping of நம (2711 to 2713), one on the letters ending karma (2714), two on the repetition சிவசிவ (2715, 2716) and a close on fixing the name in mind and tongue to end birth (2717).

2709.reading: For those whose minds melt as they contemplate the Lord as light and who clearly recite சிவாயநம, the mantra works as an alchemist's pill and he turns their bodily cage to gold.
2709.nuance: குளிகை is the alchemist's pill that turns base metal to gold, and கூடு (the cage, the nest) is the body; the image may mean a body made immortal or simply made holy. Line 1 (எளிய வாதுசெய்வார்) is hard to place: it may set those who argue lightly about the Lord against those who melt, or say the Lord is easy for those who melt.

2710.reading: Siva, Shakti, the soul, the choking impurity and maya: when the five bonds that bring ruin depart and the soul joins Siva with his Shakti, those bonds can no longer come near.
2710.nuance: The verse does not name the letters, but the five it lists are traditionally the meanings of the five letters (சி Siva, வா Shakti, ய the soul, ம impurity, ந concealment or maya). பாச மலம் ஐந்து may be 'the five impure bonds' or 'the bonds and impurity of the five'; the count is unclear, since only the last two are bonds.

2711.reading: Siva's holy name is his grace, and holds Siva, grace, the soul, concealment and impurity with maya; when Siva stands first and the rest are stilled, birth departs and the soul becomes the supreme Siva.
2711.nuance: திரோதம் is concealment, the Lord's veiling power, and நிரோதம் restraint or cessation; the verse seems to play the two against each other. The reading of the five as the letters of the name is the tradition's; சிவன் முதலாக (with Siva first) may refer to the order beginning with சி.

2712.reading: When the impurity called நம is wholly removed and that beginning left behind, by the power of the Lord's grace the faultless yoga of Siva-knowledge is attained; what one then chants is சிவாய, the truth free of impurity.
2712.nuance: நம்மலம் is read as நம + மலம், the syllables நம taken as the bonds, so that dropping the opening syllables of நமசிவாய leaves the subtle form சிவாய. It could also be read 'our impurity'. அவ் ஆதி (that beginning) is most naturally those first syllables.

2713.reading: Beginning with ந and with waking, concealment acts; when the soul stands as its own origin and reaches the end, samadhi and the fourth state become its own body, and then one may think of the syllables from ந, and samadhi, as becoming Siva.
2713.nuance: Very compressed. நமாதி (from ந-ம) and நனாதி (from waking, நனவு) are set side by side, perhaps matching the letters to the states of consciousness; துரியம் is the fourth state. The syntax of lines 2 and 4 is my guess.

2714.reading: The grace-giving mother and the father who together bore the one: when the maya within and the three impurities go and one chants சிவாய, it is those letters that end hard-to-remove karma.
2714.nuance: ஆயம் is taken here as the mother (Shakti) beside அத்தன், the father (Siva), and ஒருவனை ஈன்றவர் as their bringing forth the soul or a son; the line may also mean the mother and father of the devotee. திரிமலம் is the three impurities.

2715.reading: Those who do not come to clarity by saying Siva Siva are mutes; when the breath too, as Siva Siva, is understood and stilled within, those who stand in the clarity of Siva Siva find that Siva Siva becomes holy grace.
2715.nuance: ஊமர் (the dumb) are those who have tongues but do not use them for the name. சிவசிவ வாயுவும் may mean chanting matched with the breath, a yogic practice, or the breath itself becoming the name; I can't fix which.

2716.reading: Those of evil deeds do not say Siva Siva; when one says Siva Siva evil deeds die, one becomes divine, and the state of Siva itself follows.
2716.nuance: The plainest verse of the chapter, built on fourfold repetition. It runs both ways: evil-doers do not say the name, and saying it ends evil deeds. தேவரும் ஆவர் is 'they become gods' or 'even the gods become (so)'.

2717.reading: Hold the name நவம் still on the tongue and raise the name சிவம் in the mind, and birth ends; when even that touch is gone, the limit ends, and is not birth cut off?
2717.nuance: நவம் may stand for நம, so that the bonds' syllables are stilled on the tongue while Siva rises in thought; it can also mean 'new'. பரிசு (touch, or manner) and அவதி (limit, or affliction) are uncertain; the sense seems to be that even the act of chanting is finally left behind.

links.note: Both make the five letters an alchemy: chanting turns copper to gold in 905, and in 2709 the mantra is a குளிகை that turns the body to gold, which makes the body the metal transformed.
Both drop நம from the mantra as the soul's bound part: 1013 calls it the soul and says when it falls away the search ends, 2712 calls it impurity and leaves சிவாய as the truth free of it.

979 says சிவாய becomes the soul, its enjoyment and knowledge and ends in becoming Siva; 2711 spells out what the full name holds (Siva, grace, soul, concealment, impurity) and how the last are stilled before the soul becomes the supreme Siva.

Both free a person from deeds through the Lord's name: the Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who love his true praise, Tirumular that saying Siva Siva makes evil deeds die. Tirumular adds the converse, that evil-doers do not say it.

source_issues: 2714: line 4 reads தீர்fப்பதும் with a stray Latin 'f'; read தீர்ப்பதும்.
2717: நவம் may be a corruption of நம; the reading changes with it.
2711: நிரோதம் may be a variant of திரோதம் (concealment) rather than a deliberate contrast.
